mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate indicates an accommodative monetary policy, which may stimulate economic activity and lead to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows negative returns in more than 40% of the 20-day windows following low FEDFUNDS levels, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in the unemployment rate suggests labor market weakness, which could negatively impact consumer spending and lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 50% of the 20-day windows following an unemployment rate increase, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising unemployment and declining payroll employment indicates a weakening labor market, which could lead to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: If the S&P 500 shows positive returns in more than 40% of the 60-day windows following labor market weakness, the hypothesis is rejected.
